STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple resting on a white square plate, photographed from directly above (top-down view). It is not really a meal, just one fruit.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 26 cm across its width (a dinner-size plate). Taking the plate as ~26 cm square-ish, the area is approximately 530 cm^2 (treating it as roughly circular for the estimate, 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm^2). The apple's visible diameter is about one-third of the plate width, so roughly 8 cm, consistent with a medium apple.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole red-yellow apple (a fresh eating apple, likely Gala-type).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's top-down footprint is about 50 cm^2, roughly 9-10% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere/oblate shape of about 8 cm diameter, so volume is about 4/3 x 3.14 x 4^2 x ~0.9 (oblate) ≈ 240 ml. Using the footprint method: 50 cm^2 x 7 cm height ≈ 350 ml outer envelope; the sphere estimate is more realistic, so take about 250 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit is dense, close to water. Using a density of about 0.9 g/ml for a whole apple gives roughly 200-230 g. A medium apple typically weighs about 180-200 g, so take ~190 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple, raw, about 52 kcal per 100 g. 190 g x 0.52 = ~99 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at about 190 g and roughly 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. It covers only about 10% of the plate, consistent with a single fruit on a large plate, so the total is not inflated.
